analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: the 'Last updated' stamp (line 3) and a three-line addition near head line 985 describing landing-site test coverage (browser/RSC 404s, Markdown negotiation, agent discovery links, and their absence from human navigation and the XML sitemap). The added lines are outside the two supplied text units, which end around line 973. I relied on the patch excerpt, which is marked complete, for that addition.

This is documentation-only. It adds no executable code, endpoints, credentials, or config. It does not alter the provider/coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), the App Attest authorization boundary (TB-011), or the prefix-cache storage posture (T-041). The existing test guidance in the examined units keeps the safeguards the threat model relies on: isolated state, synthetic credentials, no production cache roots or keys, and warnings against pointing tests at production. The SSD test working volume guidance (DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR) states that it rejects relative, missing and symlink paths and that it does not change the production cache configuration or free-space checks.

The new landing-test note mentions agent discovery links being absent from human navigation and the sitemap. That is a test description, not a behavior change. I cannot verify the landing implementation or tests from the supplied evidence. Any actual landing change would need its own review, but nothing in this diff creates a security regression or invalidates a threat-model assumption. No threat-model update is required.
